parts.title: Deep sea discovery
parts.subtitle: Recent research has provided new insights into how fish communicate.
parts.article:
Deep sea discovery
 
Recent research has provided new insights into how fish communicate.
 
(A) Nico Michiels is an ecologist from the University of Tübingen in Germany who spends part of each year in Egypt, where he dives in the Red Sea, observing fish life and gathering data on its coral reefs. In September 2007 he decided to find out how far red light could penetrate the ocean depths. Seawater absorbs different colours at different depths, and as an experienced diver, Michiels was aware that red light is extinguished not far below the surface whereas blue-green light penetrates deeper. To find out the depth at which red disappeared in this particular ocean, however, he attached a special plastic filter to his dive mask, which was designed to block out all colours except red. Then he began to descend.
 
(B) In theory, once he reached about 15 metres, he should have been plunged into darkness. Instead, something totally unexpected happened. Sure enough, 20 metres down it was as dark as night. 'All the fish disappeared. With no light from the surface, they were effectively black and had become invisible,' he says. 'But it didn't stay black for long. Then I saw a group of goby fish with bright red eyes lit up against the background. After that, red spots began to show up all over the reef.'
 
(C) Even with the red filter removed, Michiels could pick them out without much trouble once his eyes grew accustomed to the gloom. It seems strange that no diver or researcher had spotted all this red before, but as Michiels points out, no one saw it because no one expected to see it. On that one dive, Michiels discovered three fish species with prominent red markings, and has found many others since.
 
(D) But how can fish appear red where there's no red light? Ordinary red pigments* look red because they reflect red light while absorbing all other wavelengths. At 20 metres down, there had to be some other explanation for the red Michiels was seeing. He suspected fluorescence. Fluorescent pigments behave differently from ordinary ones: they receive incoming light of one wavelength, for example blue, and emit light of a longer wavelength, in this case red. On the reef in the Red Sea during daytime, the most likely explanation was that the predominantly blue and green wavelengths at depth triggered the emission of fluorescent red in the fish.
 
(E) With only a week left in Egypt, and lacking the equipment to confirm that the fish were fluorescent, Michiels photographed as many of them as he could. Then, once back in Germany, he bought an assortment of tropical fish and installed them in his lab. Here he confirmed that the fish did indeed fluoresce. In most of the fish he looked at, the fluorescence could be traced to specialised pigment cells that lie in the skin beneath the scales. These cells contain 'guanine crystals', which scatter light to give fish their silvery sheen. However, Michiels says they are still not sure exactly what is fluorescing. 'It's not the crystals themselves. It's probably a fluorescent protein built into the crystals, and we have a suspicion that it might be made by bacteria.'
 
(F) Intrigued, Michiels began a systematic search for red fluorescence in reef fish. He and his colleagues, Nils Anthes and Dennis Sprenger, have identified some 50 species with red fluorescence. The most common markings tend to be on the body towards the head and to a lesser extent around the eyes, and then the fins. To Michiels, the distribution of these markings is one of the strongest indications that red fluorescence has a very particular function: communication with other members of the species. According to several recent studies, a whole range of animals employ fluorescence as a natural highlighter to boost the visibility of body parts they use to signal, for example to ward off enemies. In reef fish, the red tends to be confined to parts of the body used to signal, suggesting these markings serve a similar function. But instead of highlighting an existing colour, the fluorescence gives the fish a colour that otherwise wouldn't exist. For example, fish commonly use eye rings to signal that they are present and their direction of gaze, and Michiels suspects that red-eyed gobies use signals to indicate their location and keep their group together.
 
(G) Red light, whatever its source, doesn't travel far through water, which suggests signals are intended to be private, seen only by nearby fish of the right species. There are several lines of evidence to support this, says Michiels. And closely related species do not have completely identical markings, which suggests they might be important in species recognition.
 
(H) Michiels suspects red fluorescence has another important role for some reef fish: helping them blend in. During his first dive with the red filter, he noticed corals glow a dark but faint red too. Against this irregular red background, a fish that glows red all over would be hard to distinguish. More compelling for Michiels is the case of the scorpionfish, which lies perfectly still until food swims past, which it then sucks in.
 
(I) Yet if red plays any part in a fish's life, then it must be able to see it. Fish that live in a world dominated by blue-green light are assumed to have eyes tuned to those wavelengths, and most marine fish that have been studied are thought incapable of seeing red. One exception is the seahorse, whose eyes are sensitive to red. As for the other fish, it remains to be seen.

questions.question: During his 2007 dive, Michiels expected to encounter total darkness at about 15 metres.

analyses.content: 要注意虚拟语气“should have been”在这里表达的就是“原本预期的那样”，以及后文的“totally unexpected（完全没料到）”反证了之前的预期。
(B) In theory, once he reached about 15 metres, he should have been plunged into darkness. Instead, something totally unexpected happened.
文章B段开头明确说，根据理论（In theory），一旦他到达15米深，他“should have been（本应该）”陷入黑暗，这说明他原本的预期就是黑暗。

questions.question: Michiels could see the red markings on fish without the aid of the red filter.

analyses.content: 文章C段第一句说，即使“red filter removed（把红色滤镜拿掉）”，只要眼睛适应了昏暗，他依然能“pick them out（认出它们/看见红光）”。
不要以为滤镜是必须的，文中说滤镜是为了测试红光深度，拿掉后虽然暗，但适应后依然可见。
(C) Even with the red filter removed, Michiels could pick them out without much trouble once his eyes grew accustomed to the gloom.

questions.question: Other divers had assumed they would see fish with red markings.

analyses.content: 文章C段明确指出，从来没人发现这些红色是因为“no one expected to see it（没人预期会看到它）”，这直接反驳了题目中的“assumed they would see（假设会看到）”。
题目说“以为会看到”，文中说“完全没想过会看到”，态度截然相反。
（C段）： It seems strange that no diver or researcher had spotted all this red before, but as Michiels points out, no one saw it because no one expected to see it.

questions.question: All the fish with red markings that Michiels found during his diving expeditions came from the Red Sea.

analyses.content: 不要看到文中只提了“Red Sea”这一个地名就默认“All（所有）”鱼都来自那里，未提及不代表不存在，不要过度推断。
文中虽然重点讲了他在红海（Red Sea）的潜水���现，但并没有排除他是否在其他海域也进行过潜水考察，也没有绝对地说“所有”发现都仅限于红海。
(A) ...spends part of each year in Egypt, where he dives in the Red Sea... (F) ...identified some 50 species with red fluorescence.（文中未限制这50种全部仅来自红海这一处潜水地）

questions.question: Michiels first thought of the possibility that fish could fluoresce while he was in Germany.

analyses.content: 文章D段显示他在海里看到红光时就“suspected fluorescence（怀疑是荧光）”，E段说他在回德国“之前”因为缺少设备无法证实，说明他在埃及（潜水地）就已经有这个想法了。
分清“thought of（想到/怀疑）”和“confirmed（证实）”的区别，想是在埃及时想的，证实是在德国做的。
（D段）： At 20 metres down, there had to be some other explanation for the red Michiels was seeing. He suspected fluorescence.

questions.question: Michiels remains uncertain as to what creates fluorescence in fish.

analyses.content: 文章E段末尾提到，Michiels表示他们“still not sure exactly（依然不确定具体）”是什么在发光，只是“suspicion（怀疑）”可能是细菌制造的蛋白质。
看到“not sure exactly”对应题目中的“uncertain”，虽然有推测（suspicion），但并未定论。
（E段）： However, Michiels says they are still not sure exactly what is fluorescing. 'It's not the crystals themselves. It's probably a fluorescent protein...'

analyses.content: （F段）： The most common markings tend to be on the body towards the head and to a lesser extent around the eyes, and then the fins.
题目问“mainly（主要）”在哪，对应文中的“most common... towards the head”。
定位到F段描述红光位置的地方，文中说最常见的标记是在身体上“towards the head（靠近头部）”，其次才是眼睛周围和鳍。
文章F段中，Michiels认为这种分布表明红光有一个特定的功能：“communication（交流/通讯）”。
题目中的“specifically for... purposes”对应文中的“has a very particular function”。
（F段）： ...red fluorescence has a very particular function: communication with other members of the species.
文章F段提到很多动物用荧光作为信号，例如“ward off enemies（赶走敌人）”。
题目中的“keep ... away”是“ward off”的同义替换。
（F段）： According to several recent studies, a whole range of animals employ fluorescence... to signal, for example to ward off enemies.
（F段）： ...and Michiels suspects that red-eyed gobies use signals to indicate their location and keep their group together.
F段最后一句提到，Michiels怀疑红眼虾虎鱼（gobies）用信号来指示它们的“location（位置）”以保持群体聚集。
题目中的“show”对应文中的“indicate”。
定位到G段，文中提到“closely related species（亲缘关系很近的物种）”并没有完全相同的标记。
题目中的“very similar”对应文中的“closely related”，横线处应填名词“species”。
（G段）： And closely related species do not have completely identical markings, which suggests they might be important in species recognition.
定位到H段，文中提到“corals（珊瑚）”也会发出微弱的红光，形成红色的背景，让发红光的鱼很难被分辨。
题目问的是背景物体，文中明确说是“corals glow... red... Against this irregular red background”。
（H段）： During his first dive with the red filter, he noticed corals glow a dark but faint red too. Against this irregular red background, a fish that glows red all over would be hard to distinguish.
定位到最后一段（I段），文中说目前已知的一个“exception（例外/特例）”是“seahorse（海马）”，它的眼睛对红色敏感。
题目中的“proven to have this ability（被证明有此能力=看见红光）”对应文中的“whose eyes are sensitive to red”。
（I段）： One exception is the seahorse, whose eyes are sensitive to red.
